output.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM (
  SELECT o.customer_id
  FROM marts.fct_orders o
  WHERE o.is_revenue
    AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
  HAVING SUM(o.net_revenue) > 50000
) t;
output.explanation: The query counts customers whose net revenue in 2025 was more than 50,000 EUR. It follows the warehouse's revenue definition: only completed orders count (is_revenue = true), net revenue is after discounts, and shipping fees are left out. 2025 means orders placed from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, since the fiscal year is the calendar year. The query adds up each customer's revenue for the year, keeps those above 50,000 EUR and returns how many there are. No personal data is needed.
